title: Supervise the whole job process tree
problem: A queued script can hang or spawn children that consume shared-machine memory beyond what parent-process monitoring reveals.
mechanism: [KNOWN: historical code inspection, 2026-11-11] The neutron post-processing agent polls a script subprocess, sums resident memory across its process tree with psutil, and kills the tree when a configured time or memory limit is exceeded. The worker also limits intake using its running-process count.
finding: [KNOWN: pinned code summarized in engineering pattern A2] Resource accounting includes child processes, and a limit violation is written to the run error log. This is a polling supervisor pattern. The existing work did not execute it or establish that it prevents every resource exhaustion or process escape.

experiment.limitations: Code reading only. Polling races, transient memory spikes, child lifetime, operating-system differences and broker behavior have not been tested. This pattern does not establish a security isolation boundary.

adaptation: [INFERRED] An agent job runner can account for descendants rather than only the launcher, log the limit reason, and apply back-pressure before accepting more work. Compare this supervisor with operating-system resource controls using bounded synthetic child processes before adopting it.
unknowns: Can a short-lived or detached child escape accounting or termination at the pinned revision?
How far can usage exceed a configured limit between polls?
How do multiple workers behave when their individual memory budgets compete?
